html:
Saddam Hussein was the dictator of Iraq from 1979 until 2003. He came from a poor family near Tikrit and rose through the Arab nationalist Ba'ath Party.

After the Ba'athists took power in 1968 he ran the security services and became the real power behind President al-Bakr, whom he replaced in 1979. Oil money paid for roads, schools and hospitals, and a cult of his personality filled the country. Opponents were tortured and killed.

  • In 1980 he invaded Iran, newly ruled by Khomeini. The Iran-Iraq War lasted eight years and killed hundreds of thousands.
  • In 1988 his forces gassed the Kurdish town of Halabja, killing about 5,000 people.
  • In 1990 he invaded Kuwait. A US-led coalition drove him out in the Gulf War of 1991, and the oil fires his troops lit burned for months.

Years of sanctions followed. In 2003 a US-led invasion overthrew him. He was captured, tried by an Iraqi court for the killing of villagers at Dujail, and hanged in 2006.
sum: Saddam Hussein was the dictator of Iraq from 1979 until 2003. He came from a poor family near Tikrit and rose through the Arab nationalist Ba'ath Party.
